info.title: Corpora API
info.description: Context-Fabric MCP server + document conversion API

post.description:
Upload a source document and start converting it in the background.

Returns immediately (202) with a job id — the conversion itself has not finished yet and can take minutes for a large source (a full Bible, a multi-hundred-page EPUB). Uploads are capped at 500 MiB (413 past that); a full job queue answers 429.

**Poll vs. WebSocket:** poll `GET /convert/{job_id}` as the primary transport. `ws://…/convert/{job_id}/ws` pushes the same status object on change, but on serverless deployments (e.g. Vercel Functions) an idle socket can be killed mid-job **and a paused instance only advances the job while a request is in flight** — so on any close before a terminal status (`succeeded`/`failed`), fall back to polling; do not build a WS-only client. Neither transport reports a percentage: the converters have no progress hook, so `logs` carries a handful of coarse, fixed-stage checkpoints.

422.description: Invalid upload filename, no converter registered for `source_format`, or the upload failed pre-conversion validation — in that last case `detail` is a report object (declared/detected format, `convertible`, `reasons`, `warnings`, and a `pdf` classification payload for PDF uploads) rather than a string.

429.description: Job queue is full — retry after in-flight conversions finish.

503.description: Shared job store is unconfigured or unavailable (`JOB_STORE=supabase`).

get.description:
List the caller's conversion jobs (most recent first).

When auth is enabled, returns only jobs owned by the caller (JWT ``sub``).
When auth is disabled (``AUTH_REQUIRED=false``), returns all jobs —
capped by ``limit`` so an anonymous deployment doesn't dump the full
registry in one response. Lazy TTL reaping runs before listing so the
count stays bounded (see ``JobManager.retention_seconds``).

Poll the status of a conversion job. This is the primary status transport.

**Poll vs. WebSocket:** poll `GET /convert/{job_id}` as the primary transport. `ws://…/convert/{job_id}/ws` pushes the same status object on change, but on serverless deployments (e.g. Vercel Functions) an idle socket can be killed mid-job **and a paused instance only advances the job while a request is in flight** — so on any close before a terminal status (`succeeded`/`failed`), fall back to polling; do not build a WS-only client. Neither transport reports a percentage: the converters have no progress hook, so `logs` carries a handful of coarse, fixed-stage checkpoints.

404.description: Unknown job id — including a job that exists but belongs to a different submitter (deliberately the same response, so job ids can't be enumerated).

get.description:
Download the finished `.corpus` archive for a succeeded job.

`Content-Disposition` carries the job's `result_filename` (slugified
from the user-supplied `name`, always ending in `.corpus`) rather than
the on-disk `result_path.name` -- so the client's Save-As default is the
human-readable library name, not the server-internal `job-<uuid>` id.
`media_type` is `application/zip`: a `.corpus` archive is a zip, and an
unknown type makes some browsers treat the download as raw bytes instead
of a saveable file. 409 (not 404) until `download_ready`, matching the
`GET /convert/{id}` contract.

409.description: Job exists but is not `succeeded` yet — poll until `download_ready` is true.

get.description:
Path-level diff between two versions of the converted archive (issue #151).

``from``/``to`` accept a history row's ``id`` or ``label``; the row
marked ``current`` diffs against HEAD, any other resolves its stored
snapshot. The diff lists member paths that were added, removed, or
modified (size + CRC comparison) — no ``.tf`` content is dumped.
Read-only: nothing is bumped, snapshotted, or republished.

post.description:
Upload a document and start extracting it to a Context Fabric graph.

Returns immediately (202) with a job id; poll `GET /ingest/{job_id}` and
download the finished `graph.json` from `GET /ingest/{job_id}/download`.
`language` is the edition's BCP 47 tag (default `und` — undetermined);
`corpus_id` optionally attaches the work to an existing corpus (UUID)
instead of minting a single-document one; `name` overrides the title
Docling detects.

post.description:
Validate an archive by its format, or a dataset through the Context-Fabric cycle.

Returns 200 with ``valid: false`` and the reasons when the dataset loads but
fails validation -- an invalid corpus is a result, not a bad request. Only a
missing corpus/path/job (unresolvable target) is a 404.

get.description: Download verified current HEAD bytes, including feature edits and provenance.

What this deployment lets a client do, so UIs don't offer dead actions.

Deliberately unauthenticated (like `/health`): a client needs to know
whether to render a "Publish to the Hub" button *before* it has a token,
and neither flag is a secret -- both are already observable by making one
request and reading the 401/403. `hub_writable` is the inverse of
`HF_READ_ONLY`; `auth_required` mirrors `AUTH_REQUIRED`.

confirmation_token.title: Confirmation Token
confirmation_token.description: Required only for corpus-scope write commands (the corpora-web#100 confirmation gate); node-scope applies omit it

output_format.title: Output Format
output_format.description: Output archive: Corpus (.corpus), C-USX (.cusx) or owned TEI ZIP (.ctei). CTEI packages preserve unresolved items in review.xml.

backend.title: Backend
backend.description: Conversion engine; Python remains the default. native-experimental accepts TEI input with corpus output. Explicit category=document and the optional native wheel/runtime enable native conversion; unsupported capabilities use Python with a reason in job logs. Native parse/validation errors fail the job without retry.

category.description: Optional corpus category override (`document`/`book`/`religious`). Auto-detected from the parsed structure when omitted; an override requesting more structure than the source carries is downgraded with a warning on the job log (issue #176).

thread_id.title: Thread Id
thread_id.description: Omit to start a new thread pinned to `scope`

CitationLocator.title: CitationLocator
CitationLocator.description: An unresolved address request, never proof of an exact passage.

ConversionAccepted.title: ConversionAccepted
ConversionAccepted.description: `202` body from `POST /convert`: where to watch the job from.

total.title: Total
total.description: Jobs visible to the caller, ignoring pagination.

ConversionJobList.title: ConversionJobList
ConversionJobList.description: Page of the caller's jobs, most recent first.

source_format.title: Source Format
source_format.description: A `SourceFormat` value for `/convert` jobs; `/ingest` jobs (same registry) carry a detected file suffix instead.

display_name.title: Display Name
display_name.description: Human-readable title derived from the source document's own metadata (fallback: the request `name` / filename stem). Set once the job starts running.

logs.title: Logs
logs.description: Coarse fixed-stage checkpoints, not progress — the conversion pipeline has no percentage hook.

validation.title: Validation
validation.description: Post-conversion corpus validation summary (`corpus`/`valid`/`stats`/`reasons`/`checks`) — set once the converted archive has been checked (issue #177); an invalid archive also fails the job with the top reasons in `error`.

result_filename.title: Result Filename
result_filename.description: The filename a client should persist the result under (ends in `.corpus`, `.cusx` or `.ctei` for /convert jobs); matches the `Content-Disposition` on `/download`.

ConversionJobStatus.title: ConversionJobStatus
ConversionJobStatus.description:
One conversion job as returned by the poll/list routes.

The exact shape of `ConversionJob.to_dict()` (`jobs.py`) — declared here
(not derived from the dataclass) so the OpenAPI stops being
`additionalProperties: true` and clients can codegen against it.

CorpusCategory.title: CorpusCategory
CorpusCategory.description:
How a converted corpus is structured (written to ``manifest.category``).

- ``document`` — chapterless, few-page files.
- ``book`` — multi-chapter works (with or without front matter; cf.
  https://schema.org/Book).
- ``religious`` — bibles, qurans, books of mormon: book/chapter/verse
  (or surah) nesting.

DiffRow.title: DiffRow
DiffRow.description: One old→new pair; render with ins/del semantics + glyphs, never color alone.

DoneEvent.title: DoneEvent
DoneEvent.description: SSE `event: done` — terminal; the stream closes after this.

job_id.title: Job Id
job_id.description: UUID of the caller's completed conversion job

corpus.title: Corpus
corpus.description: Use this draft:<UUID> identifier in every AI scope

EpubLocator.title: EpubLocator
EpubLocator.description: Native resource path and opaque CFI; this core does not parse EPUB CFI.

EpubResourceLocator.title: EpubResourceLocator
EpubResourceLocator.description: An EPUB resource only, without invented fragment or CFI precision.

ErrorDetail.title: ErrorDetail
ErrorDetail.description: FastAPI's standard error body, declared so error responses codegen.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Human-readable reason, shown verbatim in the panel

current_version.title: Current Version
current_version.description: Set for `stale`: the version that superseded the scope

ErrorInfo.title: ErrorInfo
ErrorInfo.description:
Uniform error/degradation shape (also the body of 4xx/5xx responses).

`code` maps one-to-one onto the panel's degraded states:
locked → 423, stale → 409, confirmation_required → 428,
model_unavailable → 503, forbidden → 403.

message.title: Message
message.description: What is wrong, naming the node

consequence.title: Consequence
consequence.description: What the editor observes (e.g. "¶2 renders 7 slots late")

fixable.title: Fixable
fixable.description: False for slot-level corruption — those need a walker re-run, not an edit

suggestion_id.title: Suggestion Id
suggestion_id.description: Set when a Suggestion was generated for this finding

Finding.title: Finding
Finding.description: One Context-Fabric validation finding for a scoped node.

HtmlRangeLocator.title: HtmlRangeLocator
HtmlRangeLocator.description: Range spanning pinned parsed HTML text nodes; Unicode scalar node offsets.

HtmlTextLocator.title: HtmlTextLocator
HtmlTextLocator.description: Unicode selection in one text node of a pinned, explicitly parsed DOM.

ManifestUpdate.title: ManifestUpdate
ManifestUpdate.description:
Editable subset of an archive's manifest. All fields optional strings.

An empty body is rejected (422): a PATCH must change at least one field. A
field set to `""` is a legitimate value, not "unset" -- `model_fields_set`
distinguishes the two.

MessageCreateRequest.title: MessageCreateRequest
MessageCreateRequest.description: Only user messages can be posted by clients; model/tool roles are internal.

NodeAnnotation.title: NodeAnnotation
NodeAnnotation.description:
Node-correction payload: the corrected type and/or a rationale note.

An empty body is rejected (422) -- a PATCH must provide at least one of
the two. The converter's original type is recorded server-side
(`converted_otype`), never supplied by the client.

corpus.title: Corpus
corpus.description: Flat archive ID in the configured store, or job:<UUID> for an owned conversion

node_id.title: Node Id
node_id.description: Anchor node id; None only for corpus-level scope

node_type.title: Node Type
node_type.description: Corpus-specific node type of the anchor (e.g. "word", "paragraph", "chapter")

label.title: Label
label.description: Display label as the chip shows it (e.g. "doctrinam · word · Q.1 a.1 ¶1")

version.title: Version
version.description: Corpus working-version identifier the scope was captured at

content_hash.title: Content Hash
content_hash.description: sha256:<hex> of default-format text over unique selected slots in slot order, without trimming or extra separators; checked by validation and used on apply

NodeScope.title: NodeScope
NodeScope.description:
A version-pinned reference to the corpus node(s) a thread works on.

The scope is the smallest node containing the whole selection; a
selection crossing a section boundary is clamped to whole sections by
the client before it gets here (spec FR-002).

PdfQuad.title: PdfQuad
PdfQuad.description: Clockwise polygon in unrotated CropBox-relative top-left points.

ProvidersResponse.title: ProvidersResponse
ProvidersResponse.description:
What `POST /ai/chat` accepts in its provider headers.

Model calls route through the Vercel AI Gateway (an AI-SDK-compatible,
OpenAI-format endpoint). The caller supplies the provider and key
per-request via headers — `X-AI-Provider`, `X-AI-Api-Key`, and optionally
`X-AI-Model` — sourced from the user's Profile AI settings
(exegia/corpora-web#54). Keys are request-scoped: never persisted, never
logged. A missing/invalid key yields `ErrorInfo(code="model_unavailable")`.

ReferenceCreate.title: ReferenceCreate
ReferenceCreate.description: A node the user selected, optionally the last node of a same-type range.

RestoreBody.title: RestoreBody
RestoreBody.description: Restore HEAD from a stored snapshot (issue #148).

ScholarlyCitationMention.title: ScholarlyCitationMention
ScholarlyCitationMention.description:
Recognizer-supplied exact span and bibliographic lookup text.

A passage request is optional and retains the recognizer's explicit scheme.
A name or page number is never an authority for an exact target selection.

ScopeLevel.title: ScopeLevel
ScopeLevel.description: The panel's scope ladder, smallest to largest.

StoredCorpusResponse.title: StoredCorpusResponse
StoredCorpusResponse.description: One archive in the Hub storage repo (see `storage.StoredCorpus`).

rationale.title: Rationale
rationale.description: Generated rationale — the UI labels it as such

base_version.title: Base Version
base_version.description: Corpus version the suggestion was made against

content_hash.title: Content Hash
content_hash.description: Hash of the target content at suggestion time

Suggestion.title: Suggestion
Suggestion.description: A version-bound suggested change. Generated content — never corpus text.

SuggestionEvent.title: SuggestionEvent
SuggestionEvent.description: SSE `event: suggestion` — a suggested fix for the panel to render as a card.

TextLocator.title: TextLocator
TextLocator.description: Zero-based half-open scalar offsets in a named, immutable text stream.

pinned_scope.description: The scope the thread follows — navigation never re-scopes it

ThreadSection.title: ThreadSection
ThreadSection.description: A fork created by an explicit re-scope; history is kept, never replaced.

TokenEvent.title: TokenEvent
TokenEvent.description: SSE `event: token` — a batch of streamed answer text.

ToolEvent.title: ToolEvent
ToolEvent.description: SSE `event: tool` — an MCP tool call the agent made (validate, search, …).

end.title: End

UnitRange.title: UnitRange

VersionHistoryEntry.title: VersionHistoryEntry
VersionHistoryEntry.description:
The change-log record every applied change lands as, transactionally.

This is the safety net that replaces approval for now: a change that is
not recorded must not land. `resp` follows the TEI convention and always
contains both the agent and the applying user.
